shortDescription: KB Home NYSE:KBH stock gained 1.7% in Tuesday after-hours trading after the U.S. homebuilder posted stronger-than-expected fiscal Q3 earnings and in-line revenue. children: stock gained 1.7% in Tuesday after-hours trading after the U.S. homebuilder posted stronger-than-expected fiscal Q3 earnings and in-line revenue. The company also said it
of becoming a predominantly built-to-order business, with BTO homes accounting for almost three-quarters of its deliveries in Q3.
That contributed to a sequential improvement in gross profit margin. Q3 housing gross profit margin was 16.5%, up from 15.2% in Q2.

The homebuilder reaffirmed 2026 guidance for deliveries of 10.5K-11.0K (midpoint 10.75K vs. vs. Visible Alpha consensus of 10,775K ) and adjusted its outlook for housing revenue to $4.90B-$5.10B (midpoint $5.00B vs. Visible Alpha estimate of $5.09B) compared with its prior outlook of $4.90B-$5.30B.
Q4 guidance anticipates deliveries of 3.0K-3.5K vs. the 3,287K Visible Alpha consensus, and housing revenue of $1.45B-$1.65B (midpoint $1.55B) vs. $1.61B Visible Alpha estimate.

"We are operating in a housing market that continues to be challenging, with conditions weakening since our June earnings report. Higher mortgage interest rates have further pressured affordability and, together with geopolitical uncertainty and broader economic headwinds, have caused many prospective buyers to be more cautious on purchasing a home," said Executive Chairman Jeffrey Mezger. "Against this backdrop, we produced third-quarter financial results that reflected solid sequential improvement."
Fiscal Q3 GAAP EPS of $1.05, topping the average analyst estimate of $0.90, fell from $1.61 a year ago.

Revenue of $1.30B for the quarter ended Aug. 31, 2026, in line with consensus, and decreased from $1.62B in Q3 2025. Housing revenue of $1.29B, matching the Visible Alpha estimate, shrank from $1.61B a year ago.
Its average selling price of $473.0K in Q3, lagging the $473.5K Visible Alpha consensus, increased from $461.9K in Q2 and dropped from $475.7K in last year’s Q3.
Net orders of 2,604 descended 12% Y/Y from 2,950 in the year-ago period and missed the Visible Alpha estimate of 2,856.
The cancellation rate, as a percentage of gross orders, ticked up to 18% from 17% a year ago.

title: KB Home Q3 earnings top consensus as built-to-order focus bolsters profit margin
